ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral ADEF is a rhombus, and $AB=6$, $AC=4$. Then, what is the value of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \]
\[ \because \text{ Quadrilateral ADEF is a rhombus,} \]
\[ \therefore AD=DE, DE\parallel AC, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle BDE \sim \triangle BAC, \]
\[ \therefore \frac{DE}{AC}=\frac{BD}{AB}, \]
\[ \therefore \frac{DE}{4}=\frac{AB-AD}{AB}, \]
\[ \therefore \frac{DE}{4}=\frac{6-DE}{6}, \]
\[ \text{Solving gives } DE=\boxed{2.4}. \]

method.method_draft: From the image, read that D is on AB, F is on AC, E is on BC, and ADEF is ordered as a parallelogram-shaped rhombus with A adjacent to D and F. From the text, use AB=6, AC=4 and that ADEF is a rhombus. Let the common side length be s, so AD=AF=DE=s. Parameterize along the two sides from A: D=A+(s/6)(B-A), because AD/AB=s/6, and F=A+(s/4)(C-A), because AF/AC=s/4. Since a rhombus is a parallelogram, the fourth vertex satisfies E=D+F-A. Thus E=(1-s/6-s/4)A+(s/6)B+(s/4)C. But the image shows E lies on line BC, so its barycentric coefficient of A must be 0. Hence s/6+s/4=1, so s=12/5. Since DE is a rhombus side, DE=s=2.4.
